title: DEPS — Discovery 2 Phase 5B Disclosure and Revocation

sprint.name: Discovery 2 Phase 5B
sprint.scope: Fail-closed canonical Understanding disclosure and future-read revocation contract without policy infrastructure.

evidence.claimBoundary: Fourteen deterministic disclosure, revocation, isolation, compatibility, and noninterference scenarios.
Production-path audit, activation blocker, Scorecard interpretation, and rollback.
Canonical DEPS evidence and reporting rules.

scorecard.rationale: Disclosure never changes canonical truth, composition, or provenance.
Application enforcement is not activated and no user experience changes.
No collective or cross-scope protocol was executed.
Disclosure is fail-closed and revocation is separated from truth mutation.
The pure contract is deterministic, historically compatible, and exactly rollbackable.

architecture.observation: One fail-closed boundary accepts resolved decisions without owning policy.
Canonical Understanding and Runtime remain unchanged.
No canonical decision producer or durable revocation-history owner exists.

benchmarks.summary: Phase 5A authority remains the predecessor boundary.
The Phase 5B contract gate passes 14/14; application activation remains blocked.

researchObservations.observation: No benchmark research concept was promoted.

introduced: One resolved-decision envelope and one pure disclosure enforcement function.
removed: Implicit disclosure eligibility at the canonical composition boundary.
complexity.justification: The bounded contract separates disclosure from truth without a new store, service, capability, dependency, or policy system.

governanceObservations.observation: Withholding and revocation suppress future reads without changing authority or truth.

sustainabilityObservations.observation: Pure evaluation preserves determinism, compatibility, and rollback.

regressions.observation: Runtime, cognition, projection, and application behavior are unchanged.

unknownsAndUnmeasured.reason: No canonical identity, permission, membership, or policy authority exists.
No append-only decision-history owner or cache invalidation contract exists.

remainingRisks.nextBlockingDependency: Canonical resolved-decision production and durable revocation history remain unowned.
remainingRisks.remainingDiscoveryPhase: Complete Phase 5 enforcement activation before Phase 6.
remainingRisks.remainingBenchmarkGap: Application, provider, cache, audit, and distributed revocation enforcement remain unmeasured.

rollback.description: Remove the pure disclosure enforcement call; canonical Runtime and current applications are unchanged.

engineeringDecision.rationale: Accept the bounded contract while keeping application and durable revocation activation blocked.
